contract: Purpose: the owner's morning check of what Pheri did overnight. Audience: a shop owner in Birgunj, often on a phone. Primary action: approve or reject what needs them; everything else is reading. Hierarchy: the night in sentences (not tiles) > needs you (marigold) > stopped (vermilion) > ready at 8:00 (teal) > one proof sentence. Memorable detail: every claim carries a receipt chip (the customer's own words in their script, with channel and date, or the shop's order number). Palette: teal = done, marigold = needs you, vermilion = blocked or stopped, on warm paper; no cards inside cards. Viewports: 390x844 and 1440x900. Reference: the repo's own tokens (web/app/globals.css) and components (web/components/ui.tsx), adapted to a phone-first layout.

accessibility.evidence: Rendered on next start (production build). The first Tab lands on the 'Pheri' home link, and focus shows a 2px teal outline (:focus-visible in globals.css). Customer quotes carry a lang attribute (ne, hi, bho, ne-Latn), and Devanagari renders in Noto Sans Devanagari. Approve and Reject are real buttons, and the Approve tap target is at least 40px tall on 390px. The status section carries role=status, and the error screen carries role=alert. Reduced motion collapses transitions. Status colours are never the only signal: each has a word (needs you, stopped, ready at 8:00, sent). The text colours on their soft fills were set at about 6:1 (amber #8a4f00 on #fdeccb, rose #ad2f14 on #fbe4dc). Not done: a screen-reader pass with a real reader.

responsive.evidence: scripts/evidence.mjs measures document width minus viewport width for each page, at each viewport. Morning, Night shift, Slop vs Pheri, Proof and Rules all report 0 overflow at 390x844 and 1440x900, after fixing Rules: its 2-column grid and the rule input's default min-width overflowed by 504px, then 12px. At 390px the header wraps to three rows, the nav scrolls sideways when needed, and plain-vs-Pheri stacks into one column. Long Devanagari and Roman Nepali quotes wrap inside their receipts.

loading.evidence: loading-*.png: the stand-in API (scripts/empty_api.py, STANDIN_DELAY_S=10) answers the brief 10 s late. Meanwhile the header and nav are usable and three skeleton blocks (aria-busy) hold the layout, so nothing jumps when the brief arrives.

empty.evidence: empty-*.png: a night with nothing in it (stand-in API) reads 'Nothing came in overnight, so Pheri had nothing to do.' with a link to set a rule for tonight.

error.evidence: error-*.png: with the API stopped, the header and nav still render (the mode pill hides itself). The body shows 'Pheri's server didn't answer.', says nothing was sent to any customer, gives a reference and a Try again button (app/[business]/error.tsx; app/error.tsx catches layout errors).

partial.evidence: morning-*.png: one voice note is in Nepali, which Muse Voice cannot read. A marigold banner says 'Listen yourself: Rohit Ansari sent a voice note in Nepali. Muse Voice can't read Nepali yet, so Pheri didn't guess.' The rest of the night shows in full.

success.evidence: success-*.png: on Birgunj, the first card is Sita Karna's wholesale rate question: Pheri's holding reply waits with code's two choices ('Same rate as their last order' / 'You decide, and reply to them yourself'). Picking the first (taken last, after every other page, because approving changes the server's state) moves the reply to 'Ready at 8:00' marked '✓ approved by you (same rate as their last order), 08:00 their time'; need you drops from 5 to 4.

permission.evidence: permission-*.png: with PHERI_PUBLIC_DEMO=1, the brief shows 'Public demo: you're seeing a night recorded from a live run. Live runs are off here; what you approve stays in your own copy.' Approvals still work in the visitor's own sandbox.
